question: What is the primary danger of an unmanaged retained surgical needle?

options.C: Rapid elevation of systemic blood pressure
options.D: Severe allergic reaction to the suture

explanation: A forgotten needle can migrate through tissues, causing organ damage, abscess formation, and life-threatening systemic infection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why do surgical teams perform systematic needle counts during operations?

options.A: To track the exact cost of surgical consumables used
options.B: To determine when the circulating nurse should take a break
options.C: To measure how fast the surgeon is closing the fascia
options.D: To prevent accidental retention of sharps inside the patient

explanation: Counting sharps ensures that every item entering the sterile field is accounted for before the wound is closed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which surgical team member records the needle counts on the whiteboard?
explanation: The circulating nurse remains unsterile, allowing them to document counts on boards or charts outside the immediate sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: A scrub nurse's main responsibility regarding needles involves which of the following?

options.A: Tracking and inspecting every needle on the sterile field
options.B: Informing the patient about needle safety before anesthesia
options.C: Purchasing replacement suture packs from the hospital pharmacy
options.D: Disposing of used needles into municipal waste bins outside

explanation: The scrub nurse maintains direct control over the sterile area, tracking all sharps issued and returned. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: When must the initial baseline needle count take place?

options.A: Immediately after the skin is sutured
options.C: During the middle of fascial closure
options.D: When the patient enters the recovery room

explanation: Establishing an initial baseline count before surgery starts ensures all incoming items are documented. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: At what specific surgical milestone should the final needle count occur?

options.A: As soon as the surgeon requests the first hemostat
options.B: When the patient is being transferred to the theater table
options.C: During final skin closure or before dressing application
options.D: Right after the surgeon makes the initial skin incision

explanation: The final count confirms all sharps are accounted for before the surgical wound is permanently sealed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: How should the scrub nurse and circulating nurse perform the actual count?

options.A: Via text messages sent on hospital mobile devices
options.B: By guessing the total based on standard surgical trays
options.C: Silently on individual scratch pads to save time
options.D: Out loud together while pointing at each item

explanation: Counting aloud together prevents miscommunication and ensures both nurses agree on the exact tally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why is inspecting the needle tip and swage during a count essential?

options.A: To measure the exact length of the attached thread
options.B: To confirm the needle is unbroken and complete
options.C: To check if the suture material matches the hospital brand
options.D: To ensure the needle can pass through tough skin easily

explanation: Checking the physical structure ensures a broken tip has not detached and remained inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: What immediate action should the scrub nurse take when a needle count is incorrect?

options.A: Inform the surgeon to halt closure and initiate a search
options.B: Write a new number on the whiteboard to match the packaging
options.C: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask if they feel pain
options.D: Ignore the discrepancy because small needles rarely cause harm

explanation: Halting closure stops the wound from being sealed over a missing item, allowing an immediate search. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: What diagnostic tool is typically used when an intraoperative needle cannot be found?
explanation: An X-ray helps locate radiopaque surgical needles hidden within soft tissues or body cavities. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: Where should the final verified needle count be officially recorded?

options.A: Inside the patient's personal discharge envelope
options.B: In the personal diary of the operating theater cleaner
options.C: On a disposable paper towel discarded after surgery
options.D: In the intraoperative nursing documentation sheet

explanation: Official nursing records provide a permanent, legal account of intraoperative safety checks. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of poor needle count documentation?

options.A: Disciplinary action by the local nursing regulatory council
options.B: Inability to prove that standard safety protocols were followed
options.C: Severe professional liability during medical malpractice lawsuits
options.D: Improved speed and efficiency during emergency surgeries

explanation: Poor documentation does not improve speed; instead, it creates legal vulnerability and hides safety failures. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)
